construction.family: Take k renamed copies of the R44AS parent and identify all local pivot variables x2 into one shared global pivot x. All five nonpivot variables remain disjoint across blocks.
construction.children: After x=0 or x=1, the formula becomes the variable-disjoint union of k copies of the corresponding R44AS sibling A or B.

rank_theorem.proof_core: For a selected subformula S with block parts S_i, local deficiency d_i and pivot-use bit p_i, delta(S)=sum_i d_i + sum_i p_i - 1_{sum p_i>0}. Full local blocks have (d_i,p_i)=(2,1); every proper local clause-subset has d_i<=1. Thus only the full formula attains 3k-1. Child maxdef is additive under variable-disjoint union and each base child has maxdef 1.

support_lower_bound.claim: Every signed-permutation clause-subsumption transport in either sibling direction has support at least k.
support_lower_bound.proof_core: If some target block were pointwise fixed, every target clause of that block would map to the same block-variable set. Because source blocks are variable-disjoint, any source clause subsuming such an image must come from that same block. This would induce the identity local transport on the base sibling pair, which R44BQ exact replay excludes in both directions. Therefore every target block contains at least one moved variable, and the k disjoint target blocks force support>=k.
support_lower_bound.forward_existence: A B_k->A_k transport exists by applying the R44BP support-5 signed permutation independently in every block, so support<=5k.
support_lower_bound.conclusion: Minimum signed-transport support is finite in the forward direction but unbounded with k.

consequence.theorem: For every fixed constant K there exists a maxdef-critical sibling pair in this family with no signed-permutation safe-delete certificate of support <=K in either direction.
consequence.r44bq_boundary: The fixed-K polynomial discovery scheme of R44BQ is exact and useful but cannot be universally complete over maxdef-critical sibling pairs for any universal constant K.

next_admissible_math.question: Can the growing-support family still admit a polynomially discoverable signed transport by exploiting its block structure, or must the safe relation class be enlarged beyond signed permutations?
